title: bug: the JetBrains plugin ships the daemon's and proxy's devDependencies (about 168 MB uncompressed) beside 3.5 MB of runtime modules; bundle only the lockfile's production packages
description:
Files: moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts only: the prepareSandbox node_modules copies (:189-199) and a check beside requireBundledAssets (:89). No open row declares it. I checked all 38 open rows at 2026-11-02 17:53Z. .github/workflows/ci.yml is held by two WORKING rows and stays out of scope.

Origin: DONE rows promised this follow-up and nobody filed it. VSC-0 (task-a3e414a3) row D8, docs/plans/2026-11-02-vscode-reuse.md:74, reads: "Bundled node_modules ship devDependencies (vitest, typescript, rolldown) in both plugins | A follow-up to VSC-16". VSC-16 (task-6fbd0811, DONE) put it out of scope: "both plugins ship vitest and typescript today; the vsix was 61 MB at 882a4c39". This is the JetBrains half, done first. The VS Code half is a separate row that depends on this one.

Measured at HEAD 2bb683f8, from each package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3) plus `du` of the checkout's installs:
- packages/moe-daemon/node_modules: 43 dev-only top-level packages (83.8 MB) and 30 production packages (3.3 MB).
- packages/moe-proxy/node_modules: 43 dev-only packages (83.8 MB) and 1 production package, ws (0.2 MB).
- build.gradle.kts copies both trees whole into <plugin>/daemon/node_modules and <plugin>/proxy/node_modules, excluding only **/.bin/**.
- The production dependencies are chokidar, pino, pino-pretty and ws. The devDependencies are @types/node, @types/ws, tsx, typescript and vitest. In the shipped dist, the only devDependency imports (vitest) are in compiled *.test.js files, which the dist copy already excludes.

Fix: copy only the lockfile's production packages. That means every packages["node_modules/…"] entry, nested paths included, that lacks "dev": true. Keep "devOptional" and "optional" entries. Read the lockfile with the JsonSlurper the manifest code already uses.
Guard: pruning adds a new risk. A future runtime import of a dev-only package would fail only when a user starts the daemon. So the build must scan the dist .js files it actually copies (after the test exclusion) for bare specifiers: static `from '…'`, dynamic `import('…')` and `require('…')`, skipping node: builtins and relative paths. It fails, naming the specifier, when that package is not in the copied node_modules.
Error handling: the build fails with a GradleException that names the file or package when package-lock.json is missing or unparseable, when it has no packages map (lockfileVersion below 2), or when a production entry is missing on disk. It never falls back to copying the whole tree.

Out of scope:
- VS Code (moe-vscode/scripts/bundle-assets.mjs): separate row.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: held by other rows.
- The daemon's and proxy's package.json, and any npm install change.
definitionOfDone: The buildPlugin zip's daemon/node_modules and proxy/node_modules hold exactly the lockfile's production packages. No entry marked "dev": true ships, including typescript, vitest, tsx and @types/*. Every production entry ships: chokidar, pino, pino-pretty, ws and their production dependencies. The completion evidence compares an `unzip -Z1` listing against the lockfile.

The build fails, naming the specifier, when a bare import in a copied daemon/dist or proxy/dist .js file names a package missing from the copied node_modules. Prove it with a negative control in a scratch copy of the repo, never by editing the shared checkout's dist: add a non-test dist file that imports 'typescript', and buildPlugin must fail with that name.
A missing or unparseable package-lock.json, or one with no packages map, fails the build with a GradleException naming the file. Nothing falls back to copying the whole tree.

The bundled daemon loads from the unzipped plugin. `node <unzipped>/…/daemon/dist/index.js doctor --project <empty temp dir>` reaches its checklist output with no ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. It may exit 1 because .moe is missing.

`cd moe-jetbrains && ./gradlew buildPlugin test` exits 0 under the jetbrains-gradle lease. The evidence reports the zip size before and after. The shipped file set outside the two node_modules trees is unchanged.

implementationPlan.description:
Production-only copy from the lockfile, with error handling (DoD 1 and 3). Edit moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts with the Edit tool only; the GLOBAL customRule bars shell writes to tracked files.
(1) Next to the bundled* vals (:20-28), add val bundledDaemonLock = repoRoot.resolve("packages/moe-daemon/package-lock.json"), val bundledProxyLock = repoRoot.resolve("packages/moe-proxy/package-lock.json") and val distTestExcludes = listOf("**/*.test.*", "**/*.spec.*"). Use exclude(distTestExcludes) in both dist from-blocks (:185-188, :193-196), so the copy and step 3's scan share one pattern list.
(2) Beside the manifest helpers (:34-69), add fun productionPackages(lockfile: File): List<String>, parsing with groovy.json.JsonSlurper as bundleCopies does. It returns, sorted, every `packages` key that starts with "node_modules/" and whose entry is not "dev": true, as the path under node_modules ("chokidar", "@pinojs/redact", "pino-pretty/node_modules/sonic-boom"). optional, devOptional and peer entries ship, and keys outside node_modules (the "" root) are ignored. Every failure is a GradleException naming the lockfile, and none falls back to copying the whole tree:
- readText throwing java.io.IOException gives "Lockfile $lockfile is missing or unreadable: ...".
- parseText throwing (catch Exception) gives "... is not valid JSON: ...".
- A missing `packages` map gives "... has no packages map (npm lockfileVersion 2 or newer is required)".
- An entry that is not an object is an error.
- So is a key that does not fully match Regex("""node_modules/(?:@[^/\\]+/)?[^/\\]+(?:/node_modules/(?:@[^/\\]+/)?[^/\\]+)*""") or has a "." or ".." segment. This mirrors manifestString's no-.. rule, so no key can copy from outside node_modules.
- So is a non-dev entry with "link": true: a link resolves outside node_modules, and npm creates links even for optional entries (mem:gotcha-npm-lockfile-link-inbundle).
(3) Add val daemonPackages: List<String> by lazy { productionPackages(bundledDaemonLock) } and the proxy twin. They are read when prepareSandbox is configured. The lockfiles are tracked, so `test` in a snapshot without node_modules is unaffected.
(4) Replace the whole-tree node_modules blocks (:189-192 and :197-200) with one child spec per entry: daemonPackages.forEach { rel -> from(bundledDaemonModules.resolve(rel)) { into("$pluginContentRoot/daemon/node_modules/$rel"); exclude("node_modules/**") } }, and the same for the proxy. Each entry drops its own nested node_modules, because nested production entries are their own keys. A dev-only nested package therefore never ships, and nothing is copied twice. The root .bin and node_modules/.package-lock.json stop shipping: neither is a package, and Node never reads them.
(5) Rewrite the comment above the copies. It should say what ships (non-dev lockfile entries only), why (VSC-0 D8: about 168 MB of devDependencies such as typescript, vitest and tsx), and that step 3's guard checks the dist against that set.

The whole-tree node_modules copies are now per-entry child specs that exclude their own node_modules/**. implementationPlan.description:
Presence check and dist import guard, then tests by negative controls (DoD 2 and 3, plus the description's error handling).
(1) In build.gradle.kts beside requireBundledAssets (:89), add fun requireBundledPackages() and call it in prepareSandbox's doFirst right after requireBundledAssets(). It collects problems for BOTH packages and then throws ONE GradleException listing all of them, so a single run names every hit.
(a) Presence. Every productionPackages entry needs <modulesDir>/<rel>/package.json as a file. Otherwise name each missing entry and its lockfile, and say: run npm ci in packages/<pkg>. Gradle's from() of a missing directory copies nothing silently, so this check is the only thing that stops a bundle lacking a runtime package. There is no exemption for optional entries. None is non-dev today, and a platform-skipped native would ship host-only bytes, so fail closed.
(b) Imports. At script level, define val daemonDistScripts = fileTree(bundledDaemonDir) { include("**/*.js", "**/*.mjs", "**/*.cjs"); exclude(distTestExcludes) } and the proxy twin. These are exactly the dist files the copy ships, with the same Ant patterns. Read each file and collect group 2 of four Kotlin raw-string regexes:
- static: (?m)^\s*(?:import|export)\b[^'"`;]*?\bfrom\s*(['"])([^'"\n]+)\1
- side-effect: (?m)^\s*import\s*(['"])([^'"\n]+)\1
- dynamic: \bimport\s*\(\s*(['"])([^'"\n]+)\1\s*\)
- require: \brequire\s*\(\s*(['"])([^'"\n]+)\1\s*\)
Skip a specifier that starts with "." or "/" or has a URL scheme. ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*: covers every node: builtin, file: and data:. The package name is the first two segments when the specifier starts with "@", else the first segment. Skip names in val nodeBuiltins = setOf("_http_agent", "_http_client", "_http_common", "_http_incoming", "_http_outgoing", "_http_server", "_stream_duplex", "_stream_passthrough", "_stream_readable", "_stream_transform", "_stream_wrap", "_stream_writable", "_tls_common", "_tls_wrap", "assert", "async_hooks", "buffer", "child_process", "cluster", "console", "constants", "crypto", "dgram", "diagnostics_channel", "dns", "domain", "events", "fs", "http", "http2", "https", "inspector", "module", "net", "os", "path", "perf_hooks", "process", "punycode", "querystring", "readline", "repl", "stream", "string_decoder", "sys", "timers", "tls", "trace_events", "tty", "url", "util", "v8", "vm", "wasi", "worker_threads", "zlib"). That is Node 24's module.builtinModules reduced to top-level names. The dist imports fs, path, crypto, child_process, http, net, os, url, dns, zlib and async_hooks with no node: prefix, so a node:-only skip would fail on day one. Report any other name that is not a TOP-LEVEL shipped entry (one without "/node_modules/"; only those resolve from dist/) as "'<spec>' (<dist-relative invariantSeparatorsPath>:<line>)", where line is 1 plus the newlines before the match. The message reads: "Bundled <pkg> dist imports packages its bundled node_modules does not ship (devDependencies are not bundled): ...".
(2) Tests, run IN THE SNAPSHOT under the held lease, never against the shared checkout's dist (DoD 2). Copy the edited file over the snapshot's (cp /mnt/d/projexts/moes/moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts "$S/moe-jetbrains/") and cmp them. Run sha256sum on both snapshot lockfiles into $E/lock.sha256. Then run each case with cmd.exe /d /c 'set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\moe-scratch\864103f3\r\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat buildPlugin' > "$E/nc-N.txt" 2>&1. Expect a nonzero exit and the quoted names, then restore the input and run sha256sum -c:
- N1 (DoD 2). Add $S/packages/moe-daemon/dist/zz-nc.js with these four lines: import ts from 'typescript';, then import { createRequire } from 'node:module';, then const require = createRequire(import.meta.url); require('tsx');, then export const v = await import('vitest');. Add $S/packages/moe-daemon/dist/zz-nc.test.js with import ts from 'typescript'; (it must NOT be reported, because test files never ship). Add $S/packages/moe-proxy/dist/zz-nc.js with import 'vitest';. Expect one message naming 'typescript' zz-nc.js:1, 'tsx' :3 and 'vitest' :4 for the daemon and 'vitest' zz-nc.js:1 for the proxy. It must not mention node:module or zz-nc.test.js. Delete the three files afterwards.
- N2. mv the snapshot's packages/moe-daemon/package-lock.json aside; expect 'missing or unreadable' naming the file.
- N3. Make it the single character {; expect 'not valid JSON' naming the file.
- N4. Make it {"lockfileVersion":1,"dependencies":{}}; expect 'no packages map' naming the file.
- N5. mv the snapshot's packages/moe-daemon/node_modules/pino-pretty/node_modules/sonic-boom to $E/sonic-boom.moved; expect the presence message naming pino-pretty/node_modules/sonic-boom, which proves nested entries are checked. mv it back.
If a case does not fail as stated, fix build.gradle.kts in the shared tree, re-copy and cmp, and rerun from N1.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of the build.gradle.kts diff; load the adversarial-self-review skill.
(1) Scope: git diff --stat shows only moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts as yours, well under 400 net LOC. Report it in complete_step.modifiedFiles and leave peers' dirty paths alone.
(2) Disjoint child specs: every entry excludes its own node_modules/**, and nested keys copy to their own nested path. The top-level sonic-boom and pino-pretty's nested sonic-boom are different versions, and both ship.
(3) Path safety: the key regex and the ./.. check reject a crafted key such as node_modules/../../x or a backslash, and link entries are refused.
(4) Configuration vs execution: only the lockfile parse runs at configuration time. The presence check and scan run in doFirst, so `test` needs no node_modules. The lockfiles are tracked, so a test-only snapshot still configures.
(5) Scan edge cases:
- A multi-line `import {` ... `} from 'x'` matches, because the negated class spans newlines.
- An identifier like copyFrom or a call like Array.from(...) never matches: there is no word boundary inside copyFrom, and Array.from is followed by a paren, not a quote.
- CRLF dist files work.
- A specifier inside a vendored template literal (generated/skillFiles.js embeds docs/skills as 30,901 lines) would be a fail-closed false positive naming its file:line. HEAD has none. Add no allowlist.
(6) No error path falls back to copying the whole tree.
(7) Messages use invariantSeparatorsPath.
(8) Would I be embarrassed if a user's daemon hit ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND? Imports by string (pino's transport target 'pino-pretty') are invisible to the scan. They ship because they are non-dev lockfile entries, and the doctor run loads the daemon's static graph.
implementationPlan.note:
Self-review of `git diff -- moe-jetbrains/build.gradle.kts` (+112/-10, net 102; the only path of mine; peers' dirty paths left alone). The file is now 343 lines, over the 300 guideline, because the row confines scope to this file; every function is 50 lines or fewer.
(2) Child specs are disjoint: pino-pretty/node_modules/ holds only sonic-boom, and both sonic-boom versions ship.
(3) Path safety is shown by N6 (../../x), N7 (backslash) and N8 (optional link). A scope-only key would fail the package.json presence check.
(4) Only the lockfile parse runs at configuration; presence and scan run in doFirst. The gate's test task passed.
(5) Multi-line imports match. import.meta and require.resolve( do not match. The line number comes from the specifier's offset, which is CRLF-safe. A `require('x')` inside a comment or string in dist would be a named, fail-closed false positive (risk (a)); HEAD has none, since the positive gate is green, and no allowlist was added.
(6) No error path falls back to copying the whole tree.

(8) String-target imports (pino transport 'pino-pretty') ship as non-dev entries, and pino-pretty imports from the unzipped daemon dir.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: buildPlugin bundles each package's node_modules as exactly its package-lock.json non-dev entries, nested ones included. Every failure is a named GradleException, with no fallback: a missing, unparseable or packages-less lockfile, an unsafe key, a link entry, a non-dev entry missing on disk, or a bare import in a shipped dist .js file that names a package the bundle does not ship. The file set outside the two node_modules trees is unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: After-zip compare: daemon ships exactly its 31 non-dev entries and proxy ships ws. No dev entry ships, including typescript, vitest, tsx and @types/*.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
(1) Chosen: per-entry child copy specs from the lockfile's non-dev keys, each excluding its own nested node_modules. This follows the description, reuses the JsonSlurper pattern and is easy to review.
(2) Rejected: one from(node_modules) with an include Spec predicate. Gradle only descends into directories the spec admits, so the predicate would also have to admit ancestor directories such as @pinojs and pino-pretty/node_modules. That is harder to read and review.
(3) Rejected: `npm ci --omit=dev` into a staging directory at build time. It adds npm and network to the plugin build, and the row pins the lockfile approach.
(4) Rejected: reading node_modules/.package-lock.json. DoD 3 names package-lock.json.
(5) Rejected: getting builtins from `node -p require('module').builtinModules` at build time. That puts a node exec in configuration; the pinned list is deterministic.
(6) Rejected: skipping only node:-prefixed builtins, as the description literally says. The dist imports fs, path and others without the prefix, so the build would fail at HEAD.
(7) Rejected: JUnit or TestKit tests for build-script logic. They would need buildSrc or new files, and the row is build.gradle.kts only. DoD 2 and 3 define the tests as recorded negative controls, and the guard itself is the lasting regression check, which CI's buildPlugin job runs on every PR.
